plan: With 3 bidders and uniform values on [0,49], the Nash equilibrium bidding strategy for a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, which is 2/3 for n=3 bidders. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $27, so optimal bid ≈ $18. This maximizes expected profit by shading appropriately given competition from two other bidders with similar strategic incentives.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the optimal first-price auction strategy is to shade my bid to (n-1)/n of my value, which is 2/3 for n=3. This balances winning probability against profit margin. My value is $31, so I'll bid approximately $20.7 to maximize expected profit while still having a reasonable chance to win against the other two bidders' likely bids.

With 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49], the symmetric Nash equilibrium bidding strategy in a first-price auction is to bid (n-1)/n times your value, i.e., 2/3 * value. My value is $20, so I should bid approximately $13.30 to balance winning probability against overpaying. This maximizes expected profit given optimal competitor behavior.
